newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wallis report signals small bank demise - Aussie.
newsitem.headline: Wallis report signals small bank demise - Aussie.

text.p: Australia's non-bank lender, Aussie Home Loans said on Wednesday the release of the Wallis report into the financial system signals the demise of the regional banks, building societies, credit unions and small mortgage lenders.
Aussie Home Loans said the report left the door open for the country's major bank and insurance companies to grow even bigger resulting in further erosion of their services to customers.
The government-commissioned Wallis report recommended the end of the six-pillar policy between Australia's four major banks and two biggest life insurers.

However, Treasurer Peter Costello said the government would not allow mergers at this time among Australia's big four banks -- National Australia Bank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac Banking Corp and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.

"The regional banks and building societies are continuing to lose market share, as shown in recent weeks by their plummeting profits and dwlinding market share. Their only future is in mergers or being swallowed by the big banks or new foreign players," managing director John Symond said in a statement.

Aussie said that by endorsing the continuing domination of the big banking and insurance cartels in Australia, the Wallis Inquiry and government had effectively conceded the small players could no longer compete and are looking to foreign institutions and non-bank players to fill the gap.
